Every single OS integration Clicky needs (tray, transparent click-through overlay, multi-monitor screen capture, global hotkey, audio capture/playback, MP3 streaming) has a documented Electron recipe. In Tauri or WPF, half of those are \"find/write/maintain a community library.\"\n\n## Component-by-component plan (Electron edition)\n\n| Subsystem | Electron implementation |\n|---|---|\n| App shell | Main process `app.whenReady()`; no main window; tray-only |\n| Tray icon | `Tray` from `electron`; click handler shows/hides panel |\n| Dropdown panel | `BrowserWindow({ frame: false, transparent: true, focusable: false, alwaysOnTop: true, skipTaskbar: true })`, sized + positioned near tray icon |\n| Panel UI | React + Vite, custom CSS design system (port `DesignSystem.swift` tokens to CSS vars) |\n| Transparent overlay | Another `BrowserWindow` covering the virtual screen rect, `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true })`, `setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces(true)`, `setAlwaysOnTop(true, 'screen-saver')` |\n| Cursor + animations | Canvas or SVG in the overlay BrowserWindow's renderer; bezier path animation via `requestAnimationFrame` |\n| Global hotkey (Ctrl+Alt chord) | `uiohook-napi` native module — Electron's built-in `globalShortcut` doesn't support modifier-only chords reliably |\n| Audio capture | `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ audio: { sampleRate: 16000, channelCount: 1 } })` in a renderer; downsample if needed via Web Audio `OfflineAudioContext` |\n| Audio → AssemblyAI WSS | Native `WebSocket` in the renderer; send PCM16 binary frames |\n| Screen capture | `desktopCapturer.getSources({ types: ['screen'] })` → render each to an off-screen `<canvas>` → `toBlob('image/jpeg', 0.85)` |\n| Claude API client | `@anthropic-ai/sdk` directly. Use `client.messages.stream()` + `.finalMessage()`; opt into adaptive thinking + prompt caching. |\n| `[POINT:x,y]` → tool use | Replace the regex parser with `betaZodTool` — typed `{x, y, label, screen}` input schema |\n| TTS playback | `<audio>` element in main-window renderer fed by a blob URL — streams MP3 progressively, fires `ended` event |\n| ElevenLabs HTTP | Plain `fetch` to the worker `/tts` endpoint |\n| Worker proxy | Reused verbatim (`worker/src/index.ts` is portable) |\n| Auto-update | `electron-updater` with the existing `appcast.xml` format converted to electron-updater's `latest.yml` |\n| IPC main ↔ renderer | `contextBridge` exposing typed IPC handlers; renderer is contextIsolation + sandbox on |\n| Build & distribute | `electron-builder` for MSI/NSIS installer; signed with EV cert eventually |\n| Analytics | `posthog-node` in main process; same event names as macOS for dashboard parity |\n\n## Modernization wins we get for free with the SDK\n\nWhen we rewrite `ClaudeAPI.swift` as `claude.ts`, we can opt into these without extra work — see [[../api-integrations/01-anthropic-messages]] for context:\n\n1. **Adaptive thinking** (`thinking: { type: 'adaptive' }`) — Claude decides per-request. Better answers on hard questions, same latency on trivial ones.\n2. **Prompt caching** (`cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' }` on the system prompt) — ~90% cost reduction on the system prompt across turns.\n3. **Tool use** instead of `[POINT:x,y]` regex — typed, validated, language-agnostic.\n4. **Opus 4.8** as a third tier (or replacing 4.6) — most capable model, same wire format as 4.7.\n5. **Structured stop_reason handling** — surface \"refusal\" and \"max_tokens\" properly instead of silently producing half-responses.\n\nThese are tracked as port goals; we'll write them when we get to the `claude.ts` module.\n\n## Project layout (sketch)\n\n```\nclicky-win/\n├── package.json\n├── electron-builder.yml\n├── tsconfig.json\n├── vite.config.ts             # for the renderer\n├── src/\n│   ├── main/                  # main process (Node)\n│   │   ├── index.ts           # entry: tray, windows, IPC wiring\n│   │   ├── tray.ts            # Tray icon + panel show/hide\n│   │   ├── overlay-window.ts  # the transparent click-through window\n│   │   ├── panel-window.ts    # the tray dropdown\n│   │   ├── hotkey.ts          # uiohook-napi setup\n│   │   ├── analytics.ts       # posthog-node\n│   │   └── ipc.ts             # main ↔ renderer contract\n│   ├── renderer/              # renderer process (React)\n│   │   ├── panel/             # dropdown panel UI\n│   │   │   ├── App.tsx\n│   │   │   └── design-system.css\n│   │   └── overlay/           # blue cursor + waveform + bubble\n│   │       ├── App.tsx\n│   │       ├── cursor.tsx\n│   │       ├── waveform.tsx\n│   │       └── response-bubble.tsx\n│   ├── services/              # shared business logic\n│   │   ├── claude.ts          # @anthropic-ai/sdk wrapper, modernized\n│   │   ├── tts.ts             # ElevenLabs client\n│   │   ├── transcription/\n│   │   │   ├── provider.ts    # protocol interface\n│   │   │   ├── assemblyai.ts  # WSS streaming\n│   │   │   └── openai.ts      # upload fallback\n│   │   ├── screen-capture.ts  # desktopCapturer wrapper\n│   │   ├── audio-capture.ts   # Web Audio → PCM16\n│   │   └── companion.ts       # the central state machine (CompanionManager equivalent)\n│   └── shared/\n│       ├── types.ts\n│       ├── pointing-tool.ts   # Zod schema for the point_at tool\n│       └── config.ts          # worker URL, etc.\n└── worker/                    # unchanged from upstream\n```\n\n## Acceptance criteria for \"v1 done\"\n\n- App launches, lives in tray, no taskbar icon\n- Clicking tray icon opens dropdown panel\n- Push-to-talk hotkey (configurable; default `Ctrl+Alt`) captures audio\n- Audio streams to AssemblyAI via WSS, partial transcripts arrive\n- On release, screenshots all displays, sends to Claude with vision\n- Streams the response (SSE), parses tool-use for `point_at`\n- Plays TTS via ElevenLabs (`<audio>` element)\n- Blue cursor flies along bezier arc to pointed element (correct monitor)\n- Conversation history works across turns\n- Sonnet 4.6 / Opus 4.8 togglable in panel\n\nWhat we deliberately skip in v1: onboarding video, OpenAI vision fallback, Apple Speech / `Windows.Media.SpeechRecognition` offline fallback, custom keyterms, \"user-defined commands\". In Tauri or WPF, half of those are \"find/write/maintain a community library.\"\n\n## Component-by-component plan (Electron edition)\n\n| Subsystem | Electron implementation |\n|---|---|\n| App shell | Main process `app.whenReady()`; no main window; tray-only |\n| Tray icon | `Tray` from `electron`; click handler shows/hides panel |\n| Dropdown panel | `BrowserWindow({ frame: false, transparent: true, focusable: false, alwaysOnTop: true, skipTaskbar: true })`, sized + positioned near tray icon |\n| Panel UI | React + Vite, custom CSS design system (port `DesignSystem.swift` tokens to CSS vars) |\n| Transparent overlay | Another `BrowserWindow` covering the virtual screen rect, `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true })`, `setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces(true)`, `setAlwaysOnTop(true, 'screen-saver')` |\n| Cursor + animations | Canvas or SVG in the overlay BrowserWindow's renderer; bezier path animation via `requestAnimationFrame` |\n| Global hotkey (Ctrl+Alt chord) | `uiohook-napi` native module — Electron's built-in `globalShortcut` doesn't support modifier-only chords reliably |\n| Audio capture | `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ audio: { sampleRate: 16000, channelCount: 1 } })` in a renderer; downsample if needed via Web Audio `OfflineAudioContext` |\n| Audio → AssemblyAI WSS | Native `WebSocket` in the renderer; send PCM16 binary frames |\n| Screen capture | `desktopCapturer.getSources({ types: ['screen'] })` → render each to an off-screen `<canvas>` → `toBlob('image/jpeg', 0.85)` |\n| Claude API client | `@anthropic-ai/sdk` directly. Use `client.messages.stream()` + `.finalMessage()`; opt into adaptive thinking + prompt caching. |\n| `[POINT:x,y]` → tool use | Replace the regex parser with `betaZodTool` — typed `{x, y, label, screen}` input schema |\n| TTS playback | `<audio>` element in main-window renderer fed by a blob URL — streams MP3 progressively, fires `ended` event |\n| ElevenLabs HTTP | Plain `fetch` to the worker `/tts` endpoint |\n| Worker proxy | Reused verbatim (`worker/src/index.ts` is portable) |\n| Auto-update | `electron-updater` with the existing `appcast.xml` format converted to electron-updater's `latest.yml` |\n| IPC main ↔ renderer | `contextBridge` exposing typed IPC handlers; renderer is contextIsolation + sandbox on |\n| Build & distribute | `electron-builder` for MSI/NSIS installer; signed with EV cert eventually |\n| Analytics | `posthog-node` in main process; same event names as macOS for dashboard parity |\n\n## Modernization wins we get for free with the SDK\n\nWhen we rewrite `ClaudeAPI.swift` as `claude.ts`, we can opt into these without extra work — see [[../api-integrations/01-anthropic-messages]] for context:\n\n1. **Adaptive thinking** (`thinking: { type: 'adaptive' }`) — Claude decides per-request. Better answers on hard questions, same latency on trivial ones.\n2. **Prompt caching** (`cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' }` on the system prompt) — ~90% cost reduction on the system prompt across turns.\n3. **Tool use** instead of `[POINT:x,y]` regex — typed, validated, language-agnostic.\n4. **Opus 4.8** as a third tier (or replacing 4.6) — most capable model, same wire format as 4.7.\n5. **Structured stop_reason handling** — surface \"refusal\" and \"max_tokens\" properly instead of silently producing half-responses.\n\nThese are tracked as port goals; we'll write them when we get to the `claude.ts` module.\n\n## Project layout (sketch)\n\n```\nclicky-win/\n├── package.json\n├── electron-builder.yml\n├── tsconfig.json\n├── vite.config.ts             # for the renderer\n├── src/\n│   ├── main/                  # main process (Node)\n│   │   ├── index.ts           # entry: tray, windows, IPC wiring\n│   │   ├── tray.ts            # Tray icon + panel show/hide\n│   │   ├── overlay-window.ts  # main ↔ renderer contract\n│   ├── renderer/              # renderer process (React)\n│   │   ├── panel/             # dropdown panel UI\n│   │   │   ├── App.tsx\n│   │   │   └── design-system.css\n│   │   └── overlay/           # blue cursor + waveform + bubble\n│   │       ├── App.tsx\n│   │       ├── cursor.tsx\n│   │       ├── waveform.tsx\n│   │       └── response-bubble.tsx\n│   ├── services/              # shared business logic\n│   │   ├── claude.ts          # @anthropic-ai/sdk wrapper, modernized\n│   │   ├── tts.ts             # ElevenLabs client\n│   │   ├── transcription/\n│   │   │   ├── provider.ts    # protocol interface\n│   │   │   ├── assemblyai.ts  # the central state machine (CompanionManager equivalent)\n│   └── shared/\n│       ├── types.ts\n│       ├── pointing-tool.ts   # Zod schema for the point_at tool\n│       └── config.ts          # worker URL, etc.\n└── worker/                    # unchanged from upstream\n```\n\n## Acceptance criteria for \"v1 done\"\n\n- App launches, lives in tray, no taskbar icon\n- Clicking tray icon opens dropdown panel\n- Push-to-talk hotkey (configurable; default `Ctrl+Alt`) captures audio\n- Audio streams to AssemblyAI via WSS, partial transcripts arrive\n- On release, screenshots all displays, sends to Claude with vision\n- Streams the response (SSE), parses tool-use for `point_at`\n- Plays TTS via ElevenLabs (`<audio>` element)\n- Blue cursor flies along bezier arc to pointed element (correct monitor)\n- Conversation history works across turns\n- Sonnet 4.6 / Opus 4.8 togglable in panel\n\nWhat we deliberately skip in v1: onboarding video, OpenAI vision fallback, Apple Speech / `Windows.Media.SpeechRecognition` offline fallback, custom keyterms, \"user-defined commands\". All deferrable.\n\n## Reversal conditions\n\nWould flip from Electron to Tauri if:\n- Binary size becomes a marketing-level hard requirement (e.g., \"must be <25MB\")\n- A learn-Rust side benefit becomes valuable for other reasons\n\nWould flip from Electron to WPF/WinUI if:\n- Enterprise Windows-shop distribution (MSIX, Group Policy) becomes a requirement\n- Project pivots to \"native-feeling Windows tool\" over \"polished consumer ambient app\"\n\nNeither seems likely. Set via `defaultHeaders['anthropic-beta']`. |\n\n## What `respond()` does\n\n1. Build messages: history turns (text-only) + current user turn (sorted screen images each followed by their label, then the transcript).\n2.
